sources: pete-bot src/mcp-kit and its contract suite
title: One MCP kit, one set of rules for every tool I give an agent
summary: Every MCP server I run now shares one handler, one identity check and one tool contract. Read and write tiers have no destructive tier. A review caught three ways a secret could leak, and a contract suite now tests them.

stat.label: lab tools renamed verb-first, with the old names kept as aliases

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: I had several MCP servers, each with its own request handling, its own sign-in check and its own idea of what a tool looks like. Every new one repeated the same code and the same mistakes.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: The kit in pete-bot holds one JSON-RPC handler and one verifier for Cloudflare Access, which accepts a person's email or an agent's service token. A tool is a contract: a typed input, a tier, and a run function that returns a source and data. A failed read throws a typed error, which the kit turns into an error result, never an empty one.

There are two tiers, read and write, and no destructive tier. A write over MCP only files a request. A change to a host goes through the gated workflow instead. I renamed the lab tools verb-first, such as get, list, find, check and request, and kept the old names as aliases so no client broke.

rows: Return data with a named source

sections.heading: What went wrong
paragraphs: A Codex review of the kit found three redaction holes. A quoted credential escaped the filter. A password field inside an oversized object escaped it. A capped answer was cut in the middle of its JSON, which broke the envelope.
The fixes redact before serialising, redact by key name, including values made only of digits, and keep a valid envelope when an answer is cut.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: The lab server and the media server serve from the same kit. A contract suite runs against every tool and checks the tier, the error path and the redaction, so a new tool inherits the checks.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: Put the rules in a shared kit and test the kit, not each server. A reviewer who is not the author found holes I did not look for.
